name: GitLab blame provider parity (CHAOS-3722)
$limitation: This plan proves the isolated GitLab blame route's bounded traversal, Python normalization and selection, partial/rate-limit outcomes, lease fencing, and exact effect write boundary. Real ClickHouse readback is an integration proof because this sandbox cannot provide Docker; route activation and provider matrix wiring remain intentionally outside this slice.

mutations.rationale: a recursive tree that reaches the explicit page cap is incomplete and must not turn into a successful partial inventory or watermark advance
an ordinary per-file failure leaves a retryable path and must never advance the window watermark even when other files produced rows

mutations.find: if fatal := gitLabBlameFileControlError(ctx, fetchErr); fatal != nil {
mutations.rationale: a provider rate limit is a unit-level control error, not a retryable path omission; swallowing it would report an incomplete crawl as ordinary progress
GitLabCodeClient maps a missing author name to Unknown; the live Python producer must keep that canonical value through the Go row constructor
paths already present in tenant-scoped git_blame coverage must be excluded so bounded reruns advance rather than consuming the same provider quota
the active Python producer writes every blame line; dropping line content would make the sink row semantically incomplete while all identity fields still appear valid
a lease can expire after ClickHouse batch append; the sink must assert again before Send so an old worker cannot commit after ownership changes
non-rate per-file errors are explicitly best effort in the active Python producer; aborting the whole batch would lose successful later files and change retry semantics
